# VirtualList

Virtualized list with variable row heights: a long list renders only its visible part, and scrolling to the end
can load more. The height comes from the parent.

**Category**: Data · **Common uses**: Message lists, long conversation lists, search results

## Import

```ts
import { VirtualList } from 'vellum-ui'
```

## Basic usage

Of two thousand rows, only the visible part is rendered; the height comes from the parent element (in a real
page, put it in `Page fill` / `Panel fill`).

```tsx
import { Avatar, ListItem, VirtualList } from 'vellum-ui'
import { DemoFrame } from './_frame.tsx'

const people = Array.from({ length: 2000 }, (_, i) => ({ id: String(i), name: `Member ${i + 1}` }))

export function Basic() {
  return (
    <DemoFrame>
      <VirtualList
        items={people}
        getKey={(p) => p.id}
        renderItem={(p) => <ListItem leading={<Avatar name={p.name} size={28} />} title={p.name} />}
      />
    </DemoFrame>
  )
}
```

`DemoFrame` is only a fixed-height container of the examples; in a page, put the component in `Page fill` or `Panel fill`.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Description | Default | Required |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `items` | `readonly T[]` | The data. | — | Yes |
| `getKey` | `(item: T, index: number) => string` | Stable key of a row (such as the message ID). | — | Yes |
| `renderItem` | `(item: T, index: number) => ReactNode` | Renders a row. | — | Yes |
| `estimateSize` | `number` | Estimated row height in pixels, 48 by default. | — | No |
| `overscan` | `number` | Number of extra rows rendered outside the visible area (overscan), 6 by default. | — | No |
| `onReachStart` | `() => void` | Called when scrolled near the top (to load earlier data). | — | No |
| `onReachEnd` | `() => void` | Called when scrolled near the bottom. | — | No |
| `empty` | `ReactNode` | Shown when there are no items. | — | No |
| `aria-label` | `string` | Accessible name. | — | No |
| `data-testid` | `string` | Test ID for locating the element in tests. | — | No |

Does not accept `style` or `className`: appearance is adjusted only through the semantic props above and the theme.
